items.reason: Awkward tail 'that had been embalmed in it that way' — 'in it that way' reads as a stumble aloud; the sense is simply that they were embalmed in the ambergris.
items.new: I forgot to mention that we found some hard, round, bony plates in this ambergris. At first Stubb thought they might be buttons off sailors' trousers, but it later turned out that they were just pieces of small squid bones that had been embalmed in it.

items.reason: 'ruthless hands passed it every hour' can be read as hands handing the coin around; the point is that ruthless hands passed by it. Clarify the verb so listeners do not reread.
items.new: Now this doubloon was of the purest virgin gold, dug somewhere out of the heart of splendid hills from which the headwaters of many a Pactolus (the gold-bearing river of legend) flow east and west over golden sands. And though it was now nailed among rusty iron bolts and copper spikes green with verdigris, it still kept its Quito glow, untouched and unstained by any filth. It had been placed among a ruthless crew, ruthless hands passed by it every hour, and all night long it was wrapped in thick darkness that could have hidden any thief creeping up on it; yet every sunrise found the doubloon where the last sunset had left it. For it was set apart and made sacred for one awe-inspiring purpose, and however reckless their sailor ways, the sailors one and all revered it as the white whale's talisman. Sometimes they talked it over during the weary night watch, wondering who would end up with it, and whether he would live to spend it.

items.reason: 'He pulled it out' has no antecedent (previous paragraph is just the hail), so the reader must reread to learn 'it' is the arm. Reorder so the object is named before the pronoun.
items.new: "Do you see this?" From the folds that had hidden it, he drew out a white arm made of sperm whale bone, ending in a wooden head like a mallet, and held it up.

items.reason: Second sentence ('it seemed not only to be trying in every way to avoid showing itself outwardly in the slightest, but inwardly as well to be more than half unsure of itself') forces a reread: the 'not only...but inwardly as well to be' structure is unbalanced. Rebalanced with minimal change; restores source's 'almost seemed'.
items.new: "Captain Ahab," said the mate, flushing as he stepped farther into the cabin. His boldness was so oddly respectful and careful that it almost seemed not only to be trying in every way to avoid the slightest outward show of itself, but also, inwardly, to be more than half unsure of itself. "A better man than I am might well overlook in you what he would be quick enough to resent in a younger man — yes, and in a happier one, Captain Ahab."

items.reason: 'But when Ahab looked up, he slipped away to one side' — 'he' reads as Ahab; it is the Parsee who slips away.
items.new: When that was done, Perth was about to start welding the twelve into one, but Ahab stopped him and said he would weld his own iron. So Ahab hammered away on the anvil with steady, gasping grunts, while Perth handed him the glowing rods one after another and the hard-driven forge sent up its fierce, straight flame. Meanwhile the Parsee passed by without a word and bent his head toward the fire, as though calling down some curse or some blessing on the work. But when Ahab looked up, the Parsee slipped away to one side.
